title: Preaching on the trumpet and a style made of everyone
summary: He recalls his Nashville preacher act with plunger, hat and mock Bible, and says his style is a combination of everybody he heard.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: them all night long. But I listened to these guys, they all had something great about them. About their playing, so I wanted to be able to play with them and I did play with them and last -- night before last I played with, as I said, Clark Terry, I worked with him, played with him and the night before last I was at a seminar, I played with Thad Jones and Jimmy Owens. Now we had -- went on individually, we gave our history of what we're playing and our style of playing and so we did solo play, like I preached on the trumpet, like I used to go out on jobs because they wanted to hear me preach. On the trumpet, Now they don't do that today.

They said bring the boy that preaches, so I'd go out on a job and preach with a plunger and a mute and I put a hat on my head, some specs and I had a book like it was a bible, and that was the act that I had. And they would have me preaching. They thought that was great in Nashville, in those days. So I learned to do that. And I demonstrated that that over there the other night, about preaching and I showed them how it's done and all that stuff and then up to date -- I told them -- my style of trumpet playing, I guess, is a combination of everybody I've heard in my life.
